title: The H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience Framework
subtitle: A Research Report on Reducing Human and Systemic Vulnerability to Interconnected Global Crises
description: A development-oriented framework for understanding, reducing and preventing vulnerability to interconnected global crises through coordinated, sustainable…
contribution: Integrates interconnected systemic risk analysis with a coordinated six-layer, eight-pathway programme of structural vulnerability reduction, a five-step Development-to-Resilience Cycle, and a ten-dimension measurement architecture.
abstract: The H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience Framework (HH-2026-94, 41 pages), developed and formalized by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics, as a proposed synthesis open to testing and correction.

keyFindings.title: Interconnected crises require interconnected solutions: interventions must be evaluated for their effects on other systems.
Vulnerability reduction is a primary objective of resilience: improving underlying conditions reduces exposure, sensitivity and susceptibility to future crises.
Development is a mechanism of prevention: infrastructure, healthcare, education, energy, income and institutions reduce the consequences of many threats at once.
Sustainable convergence is essential: economic and technological advancement must proceed alongside environmental improvement and stronger human development.
Resilience is cumulative and long-term: coordinated improvements create reinforcing cycles that progressively strengthen the capacity to withstand disruption.
